He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia Cavaliers]], where in 2019 he was the starting [[shooting guard]] on [[2018–19 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|their national championship team]]. Jerome was drafted by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in the [[2019 NBA draft]] but was traded to the [[Phoenix Suns]]. He has also played for the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]], [[Golden State Warriors]] and [[Cleveland Cavaliers]]. ==Early years== During his early childhood, Jerome played for [[Riverside Church]] in [[Amateur Athletic Union|AAU]] with [[Donovan Mitchell]].{{cite news | last = | first = | date = November 5, 2018 | title = The Road Home: Men's Basketball - Ty Jerome | url = https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2rAco7pbwGA | work = [[Virginia Cavaliers|Virginia Sports TV]] | access-date = 2025-05-15 }}{{cite news | last = Flickinger | first = Jackson | date = November 27, 2024 | title = Donovan Mitchell and Ty Jerome’s on-court chemistry dates back to getting cussed out as kids | url = https://www.fearthesword.com/2024/11/27/24307160/cavs-donovan-mitchell-and-ty-jeromes-on-court-chemistry-dates-back-to-getting-cussed-out-as-kids-nba | work = [[SB Nation]] | access-date = 2025-05-15 }} Jerome played high school basketball at The [[Masters School]] in [[Dobbs Ferry, New York]]. He attended [[Iona Preparatory School]] in [[New Rochelle, New York]] for high school, playing varsity for all four years. After his junior season at Iona Prep, he was named first-team All-Conference, All-Metropolitan, and All-State.{{cite web |title=Virginia Cavaliers Bio |url=https://virginiasports.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=255 |website=virginiasports.com |access-date=February 9, 2019}} Jerome's senior season was cut short due to a hip injury.{{cite web |last1=Santos |first1=Dylan |title=Ty Jerome of Iona Prep, a Virginia signee, to miss rest of HS season because of pending hip surgery freshman year at Virginia, Jerome was the backup point guard to [[London Perrantes]]. Coming off the bench, he averaged 4.3 points, 1.6 rebounds, and 1.5 assists. Jerome took over as the Cavaliers' starting point guard his sophomore year. On December 30, 2017, he put up a career-high 31 points against [[Boston College Eagles men's basketball|Boston College]]. His play during the season earned him a spot on the [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball teams|All-ACC]] Third Team. Prior to the [[2018–19 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2018–2019 season]], Jerome was selected to the [[2018–19 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season#Preseason All-ACC Teams|pre-season all-ACC Second Team]].{{cite web |title=DUKE TOPS ACC BASKETBALL PRESEASON MEDIA POLL |url=https://theacc.com/news/2018/10/25/mens-basketball-duke-tops-acc-basketball-preseason-media-poll.aspx |website=theACC.com |access-date=February 9, 2019 |date=October 25, 2018}} On February 4, 2019, Jerome was named as one of the ten finalists for the [[Bob Cousy Award]], recognizing the nation's top college point guard. He was projected in most mock drafts as an early second-round pick in the [[2019 NBA draft]].{{cite web |last1=Darney |first1=Caroline |title=Ty Jerome named a finalist for the Bob Cousy Award |url=https://www.streakingthelawn.com/2019/2/5/18210820/ty-jerome-finalist-bob-cousy-award-back-injury-update |website=streakingthelawn.com |publisher=Vox Media, Inc |access-date=February 9, 2019 |date=February 5, 2019}} Jerome averaged 13.6 points per game and 5.5 assists per game, helping lead Virginia to another #1 seed in the [[2019 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament|2019 NCAA tournament]]. Virginia would win the [[2019 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Championship Game|2019 Championship game]] 85–77 behind Jerome's 16 points, 8 assists, and 6 rebounds. At the conclusion of the season, Jerome announced his intention to forgo his final season of collegiate eligibility and declare for the [[2019 NBA draft]] while hiring an agent.{{Cite news|url=https://www.richmond.com/sports/college/schools/university-virginia/uva-basketball-star-ty-jerome-will-leave-school-early-for/article_67c22cd7-e669-57a8-89fe-eb0fd4728918.html|title=UVA basketball star Ty Jerome will leave school early for the NBA Draft|work=[[Richmond Times-Dispatch]]|author=Mike Barber|date=April 15, 2019}} ==Professional career== ===Phoenix Suns (2019–2020)=== On June 20, 2019, the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] selected Jerome with the 24th pick in the [[2019 NBA draft]]. His rights were later traded to the [[Boston Celtics]] alongside Philadelphia's 33rd pick for the draft rights to [[Matisse Thybulle]]{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/thybulle-team-gets-pick-checks-many-key-boxes|title=In New Picks, Team Lands Prospects Who Check Key Boxes|date=June 21, 2019|work=NBA.com|access-date=June 21, 2019}} before being traded to the [[Phoenix Suns]] alongside [[Aron Baynes]] for a future first round pick.{{cite web|title=Celtics Complete Trade With Phoenix Suns|url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-complete-trade-phoenix-suns|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 6, 2019|date=July 6, 2019}} Coincidentally, both players the Suns traded for were recruited out of high school and played their college basketball for [[Tony Bennett (basketball)|Tony Bennett]]: Baynes at Washington State and Jerome at Virginia. On July 6, the Suns announced that they had signed Jerome.{{cite web|title=Suns Sign Johnson, Jerome, Lecque|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/suns-sign-johnson-jerome-lecque|date=July 6, 2019|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 6, 2019}} Before the start of the season, Jerome sprained his right ankle on October 21, leaving him out indefinitely.{{cite web|title=Injury update: Suns guard Ty Jerome|website=[[NBA.com]]|url=https://www.nba.com/article/2019/10/24/ty-jerome-injury-update-official-release|date=October 24, 2019|access-date=November 26, 2019}} On November 25, Jerome was a day later. ===Oklahoma City Thunder (2020–2022)=== On November 16, 2020, Jerome was traded to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] alongside [[Kelly Oubre Jr.]], [[Ricky Rubio]], [[Jalen Lecque]], and a 2022 first-round pick in exchange for [[Chris Paul]] and [[Abdel Nader]].{{cite web |title=Thunder Acquires Ty Jerome, Jalen Lecque, Kelly Oubre Jr., Ricky Rubio and 2022 First-Round Draft Pick Jerome Gets 8 Minutes in G League Game]". [[CBS Sports]], February 12, 2021. Accessed February 16, 2021 He made his debut playing limited minutes for the Blue on February 11, 2021. Jerome made his Thunder debut in a game against the [[Atlanta Hawks]] on February 26. He finished the game with nine points, five rebounds, and seven assists in 22 minutes played in a 118–109 win over the [[Atlanta Hawks]]. His seven assists also set a record for the most assists in a debut in Thunder franchise history.{{cite 23-24 Roster (cropped) JEROME.png|thumb|Jerome in 2023]] On July 6, 2023, Jerome signed with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/releases-niang-jerome-signing-230706|title=Cavaliers Sign Georges Niang and Ty Jerome|work=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2023}} He played in only 15 minutes across two games for Cleveland before suffering a right ankle impingement in an October 27 games against the [[2023–24 Oklahoma City Thunder season|Oklahoma City Thunder]].{{Cite web|title=Cavaliers ride Ty Jerome heater to Game 1 win over Heat|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/44775963/cavaliers-ride-ty-jerome-heater-game-1-win-heat|access-date=April 24, 2025|website=espn.com|date=April 21, 2025 |language=en}} On January 25, 2024, Jerome underwent successful right ankle surgery and missed the remainder of the season.{{Cite web|title=Cavaliers' Ty Jerome Undergoes Successful Right Ankle Surgery|url= https://www.si.com/nba/cavaliers/news/cleveland-cavaliers-ty-jerome-undergoes-successful-right-ankle-surgery|access-date=April 24, 2025|website=si.com|date= January 26, 2024|language=en}} On November 20, 2024, Jerome scored 27 of a season-high 29 points in the first half of the Cavaliers' 128–100 win over the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].{{cite news |title=Cavaliers 128-100 Pelicans (Nov 20, 2024) Game Recap |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401704818 |access-date=21 November 2024 |work=ESPN |date=20 November 2024 |language=en}} On January 24, 2025, he would score a new career-high with 33 points made (including a perfect 8-of-8 shooting rate for three-point shots) off the bench in a 129–132 loss to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]]. Jerome ended up becoming the first Cavaliers player in franchise history to make eight three-pointers without missing a single attempt.{{Cite web|title=Ty Jerome's career night spoiled as Cavs lose to 76ers, 132-129|url=https://www.cleveland.com/cavs/2025/01/ty-jeromes-career-night-spoiled-as-cavs-lose-to-76ers-132-129.html?outputType=amp|access-date=January 27, 2025|website=cleveland.com| date=January 25, 2025 |language=en}} On April 19, 2025, Jerome made his playoff debut during the first round of the playoffs, scoring 28 points alongside five rebounds and three assists in a 121–100 Game 1 win over the [[Miami Heat]].{{Cite web |title=Mitchell, Jerome help Cavaliers rout Heat 121-100 in Game 1 of 1st-round series |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401767816 |access-date=April 28, 2025 |website=ESPN}} === Memphis Grizzlies (2025–present) === On July 14, 2025, Jerome signed a three-year, $28 million contract with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].{{Cite web |date=July 14, 2025 |title=Memphis Grizzlies Sign Guard Ty Jerome |url=https://www.instagram.com/p/DMGzcRwSuXQ/?igsh=MWxpZ243NDdrM3R6Zg==}} On October 20, Jerome was ruled out for at least four weeks strain|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/46664467/grizzlies-new-guard-ty-jerome-sidelined-calf-strain|access-date=January 22, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} On November 22, it was reported Grizzlies and season debut, scoring a team-high 20 points in a 131-114 loss to the [[2025–26 Minnesota Timberwolves season|Minnesota Timberwolves]].{{Cite web|title=Grizzlies' Ty Jerome: Pops for
